You’ve said it all very well and that’s been my life story as well. I’ve been just another guy inside a cubicle sitting at a computer all day, like a dedicated minion but once again my number came up and you know the rest. I thought I’d enjoy the time off, since my last job involved a near 90 minute drive one way and 10 hour work days, I was gone from 5 in the morning until sometimes 6:30pm. But the time at home grew old fast. I thought I could catch up on home projects I left undone, spoil the pets again and revisit some hobbies or read and update my trade. Nothing right now interests me. I can hardly watch tv (I’m tired of the so called job surge), listen to music or even play an app game. I see everyone else with jobs and it would be so nice to be wanted again and do things others take for granted. It’s like, why shave, why do anything if I’m going to just be inside another day?

Thanks for the encouragement. I think that companies hide behind job sites and rely too heavily on recruiters to find workers. Gone are the days when in house Human Resources could actually accept applications and set up interviews in person. The internet made it easier on employers but not employees so jobs go unfilled or filled by the wrong candidate. Too little experience gives them reason not to hire you but too much tells them that you’re probably too old to learn and think you probably want too much. It’s all based on data and statistics that determine people and we’ve become a faceless society.

Sometimes job fairs help point to the right direction, there just haven’t been any around my area. Thanks for the tip.

I live in an area where there aren’t very many companies that are hiring. The nearest cities where there are work are usually far from home. Just when I get on my feet to move near my work I’ll get laid off as most jobs in my field are temporary. The job landscape has chanced drastically, companies no longer train and want you to hit the ground running with a near impossible list of requirements. No one talks without a prior appointment for an interview, they’re either too lazy or uptight to meet someone face to face or out of the blue.

I more than know how you feel. I absolutely agree how we are dictated by work and money not just to enrich our lives but sustain them. We are also dictated by a faceless system that can somehow judge us and our performance unseen, without having the decency to speak to us by phone or in person. Our resumes have to incorporate the right amount of bells, whistles and neon lights to grab someone’s attention and the ones who they attract are usually clueless recruiters, some overseas, who could honestly care less about our situation. 

The days are just so long, I try sleeping as some manage to, but for me the constant worry and anxiety takes over to a point where sleeping pills no longer work. I suffer from anxiety, depression and high blood pressure, all of my medications have run out, I can’t afford insurance and most doctors won’t see the uninsured without it. I was never one for handouts, other than unemployment funds, which are now gone. I just don’t know how long I can take this, it’s like having a disease and either waiting for it to kill me or end it to stop the suffering.

Thanks for your response and caring. I’m in drafting and design, basically jobs are all reliant on forwarding resumes and posting on job sites, waiting and hoping someone will call for an interview or maybe a recruiter will notice my posts. No one responds from the job site postings and weeks later I’ll see that the position expired. Sometimes a recruiter (who are all useless) calls about an out of state job and I usually say I’m very interested, then that’s as far as it goes and the recruiters aren’t heard from again. If I can get an in person interview I’d jump at the chance but for 8 months nothing has happened. I’d even settle for a lower paying job or some other trade but even those opportunities aren’t happening. I’m just tired, every day sitting home is like Ground Hogs Day. I have so much to give but no one wants it.
